headline_marked: ICT-1 to deliver [[verdict on June 28 in Rampura killings case]]
headline: ICT-1 to deliver verdict on June 28 in Rampura killings case
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal will rule on charges of crimes against humanity regarding the shooting of two people during the 2024 July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has set June 28 as the date for the verdict in a case involving crimes against humanity. The case concerns the shooting and killing of two people, including a youth who was hanging from a building's cornice in Dhaka's Rampura during the 2024 July Uprising.
A three-member bench led by Chairman Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder delivered the order after the second round of arguments were completed on Monday.

Five suspects are named in the case, including former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman and former Rampura Police Station chief Md Mashiur Rahman. Only one suspect, Chanchal Chandra Sarkar, has been arrested and was present in court.
The other four suspects remain absconding. The prosecution's chief counsel, Md Aminul Islam, has rejected the defense arguments and sought the maximum punishment for all accused.
The trial had previously seen a postponement from March 4 after the prosecution requested to submit new digital evidence, which led to the first witness, Amir Hossain, testifying again.
caption:

A three-member bench led by Chairman Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder delivered the order after the second round of arguments were completed on Monday.

Five suspects are named in the case, including former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman and former Rampura Police Station chief Md Mashiur Rahman. Only one suspect, Chanchal Chandra Sarkar, has been arrested and was present in court.

The other four suspects remain absconding. The prosecution's chief counsel, Md Aminul Islam, has rejected the defense arguments and sought the maximum punishment for all accused.

The trial had previously seen a postponement from March 4 after the prosecution requested to submit new digital evidence, which led to the first witness, Amir Hossain, testifying again.

headline_marked: FM terms [[Adviser Zahed's Delhi airport incident]] 'regretful'
headline: FM terms Adviser Zahed's Delhi airport incident 'regretful'
summary: Prime Minister’s Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman returned to Bangladesh after being flagged and delayed for hours by Indian immigration at Indira Gandhi International Airport.
details: Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman has described the return of Prime Minister’s Adviser on Policy and Strategy Affairs Zahed Ur Rahman from Delhi as "unexpected and regretful".
The incident occurred at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport, where Dr. Zahed was reportedly kept waiting for hours by Indian immigration authorities.
According to reports, he was flagged during routine security checks when his name appeared on a watchlist, leading to questioning and a delay of approximately two and a half hours.
Although Indian authorities eventually allowed him to proceed, Dr. Zahed decided to return to Bangladesh instead of continuing his visit.
Dr. Zahed had travelled to New Delhi to attend the 28th Meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials (CSO) of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA).
He was travelling on a regular Bangladeshi passport with a SAARC visa, and the Bangladesh High Commission had officially informed India’s Ministry of External Affairs of his visit.
Bangladesh High Commissioner to India Riaz Hamidullah reportedly went to the airport to receive him during the incident.
Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman stated that the foreign ministry is taking appropriate measures and will clarify its position by the end of the day.
caption:
A Bangladeshi Adviser to the Prime Minister was flagged and delayed for hours at Delhi airport before deciding to return home.

Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman has described the return of Prime Minister’s Adviser on Policy and Strategy Affairs Zahed Ur Rahman from Delhi as "unexpected and regretful".

The incident occurred at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport, where Dr. Zahed was reportedly kept waiting for hours by Indian immigration authorities.

According to reports, he was flagged during routine security checks when his name appeared on a watchlist, leading to questioning and a delay of approximately two and a half hours.

Although Indian authorities eventually allowed him to proceed, Dr. Zahed decided to return to Bangladesh instead of continuing his visit.

Dr. Zahed had travelled to New Delhi to attend the 28th Meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials (CSO) of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA).

He was travelling on a regular Bangladeshi passport with a SAARC visa, and the Bangladesh High Commission had officially informed India’s Ministry of External Affairs of his visit.

Bangladesh High Commissioner to India Riaz Hamidullah reportedly went to the airport to receive him during the incident.

Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman stated that the foreign ministry is taking appropriate measures and will clarify its position by the end of the day.
